description: Governed scope of runtime verification and validation (VDR-TFR-MVX, VDR-TFR-PDD, FRC-CSX-VVK). Every inventory component type is either a machine type, which the runtime emitter (infrastructure/lambda) must re-validate live against the deploy gate's policy within max_age_hours, or an excluded type with the reason another mechanism covers it. Reconciliation invariant (m) in scripts/reconcile.py reads this file, fails closed on any component type it does not classify, and is run by evidence-nightly.yml against the published inventory and runtime signal.
rationale: VDR-TFR-MVX requires machine-based resources to be verified and validated at least every 3 days, so a machine component counts as validated only by an assessed runtime validation (no unread attribute) younger than 72 hours. VDR-TFR-PDD requires drift detection at least every 14 days on resources likely to drift; every machine type is re-validated daily, so the likely-to-drift set is recorded for the drift report and the 14-day window is met with margin. Software packages and site pages are not machine resources in this sense: their state is fixed by the deployed artifact, which is re-scanned (Syft and Grype, twice daily) and re-hashed (every deploy), and the runtime package-integrity check proves the deployed code is still that artifact.

object_store.why: Bucket encryption, versioning, public-access block and tags can be changed in the console or by any principal with bucket rights.

cdn_distribution.why: Managed by the operator-applied bootstrap stack and editable in the console; protocol policy and TLS floor can change outside the deploy.

function.why: Code and configuration can be updated directly (UpdateFunctionCode/Configuration) outside the deploy; the package-integrity check compares the live code hash with the inventoried one.

iam_role.why: Trust and attached policies are the highest-value change an intruder or a hurried operator makes outside Terraform.

iam_policy.why: Inline policies can be edited in the console; privilege creep is the drift that matters most.

iam_group.why: The operator groups carry hand-attached managed policies (bootstrap stack, applied by hand).

oidc_provider.why: Audience list changes would widen who can federate into the deploy roles.

identity_provider.why: MFA, password and sign-up settings of the user pool are console-editable.

api_gateway.why: Routes, authorizers, throttling and access logging are console-editable and govern the app's exposure.

kms_key.why: Keys can be disabled, scheduled for deletion or have rotation turned off.

secrets_manager.why: Rotation lapses with time even when nobody touches the secret.

tls_certificate.why: Validity runs out with time; renewal can fail silently.

dns_zone.why: DNSSEC signing can stop (key state, registrar) without any Terraform change.

audit_log_trail.why: Logging can be stopped with one API call (StopLogging), a classic intruder step.

log_group.why: Created and changed only by Terraform; retention and key are still re-validated daily.

event_schedule.why: Created and changed only by Terraform; a disabled schedule is still caught daily.

notification_topic.why: Created and changed only by Terraform; encryption is still re-validated daily.

metric_alarm.why: Created and changed only by Terraform; disabled actions are still caught daily.

message_queue.why: Created and changed only by Terraform; encryption is still re-validated daily.

kv_table.why: The state-lock table is created by the bootstrap stack and not otherwise touched; point-in-time recovery is still re-validated daily.

excluded_types.npm_package: Software, not a machine resource: its content is fixed by the lockfile integrity hash in the deployed artifact. Covered by Syft and Grype twice daily (evidence-nightly.yml) and by the runtime package-integrity check of the function that ships it.
excluded_types.pypi_package: Software, not a machine resource: fixed by the deployed artifact. Covered by Syft and Grype twice daily and by the runtime package-integrity check of the function that ships it.
excluded_types.html_artifact: Static content, not a machine resource: hashed into the inventory and scanned for accessibility on every deploy; the bucket that serves it is a machine component.
excluded_types.external_service: A third party outside the boundary (Sigstore, GitHub, the vulnerability feeds, the MFA provider): this system cannot read its configuration. Tracked in data/third-party-components.json.
